描述_EN: 1733), who owned over twenty thousand pieces. dehua was the second largest producer of ceramics, including export ware, after jingdezhen. moulded and finished by hand, these figures were usually placed on household altars and worshipped as devotional images in china. porcelain figures of guanyin, the buddhist goddess of compassion, were popular products of the dehua kilns in fujian province, south-east china. during the17th century they became popular in europe, where the body and colour of the dehua ware, also known as 'blanc de chine', were much admired. the figures were placed on tables and cabinets in the residences of aristocrats and wealthy people, or exhibited in the so-called 'porcelain rooms', where walls and niches were completely filled with large quantities of ceramics. one of the most important european collections of this type belonged to augustus the strong of saxony (d.
